title: 53% of Americans Spend Too Much Time on Phones
paragraphs: Do you think you spend too much time on your phone? If so, you are not alone. According to a new survey by the Pew Research Center, more than half of American adults feel the same way.
The survey was carried out between May 26 and June 1, 2026. It asked 9,750 adults in the United States about how they use their smartphones.

The survey found that 53% of American adults believe they spend too much time on their smartphones. About a third said that the amount of time they spend on their phones is about right, while only 3% said they spend too little time.

Younger people were much more likely to feel that they use their phones too much. Among adults aged 18 to 29, 70% said they spend too much time on their phones. This fell to 64% among people aged 30 to 49 and 49% among those aged 50 to 64. Among people aged 65 and older, only 25% felt this way.

Many people have tried to change their habits. Around 45% said they had tried to cut back on their phone use in the past 12 months. However, only about a quarter of those who tried said they had been very successful. Most said they had only partly succeeded or that little had changed.

The survey also asked about the effects of phones on people's lives. About 41% of adults said that using their smartphone hurt their sleep, while only 5% said it helped. On the other hand, 73% said their phone helps them stay informed.

According to the researchers, scrolling, notifications and messages make it hard for people to put their phones down. Some experts also believe that features such as videos that play automatically and push notifications are designed to keep people using their phones for as long as possible.
